problem_type: local media public-reachability and provider upload capability routing
symptom: A local reference image, video, or audio file can fail generation because the selected anonymous host or image-only upload endpoint is unavailable, rejects the media, or returns an expiring value the target provider cannot use.
direct_cause: Multiple callers invoke asset localization with provider-specific or incomplete ingestion declarations, while the shared declaration type cannot represent two-stage uploads, raw PUTs, or non-Bearer provider keys.
class_root: There is no single capability-driven upload contract that all generation entry points use to select a media-compatible, lifecycle-safe channel before the paid provider request.
affected_population: Users sending local image, video, or audio references through ordinary HTTP mappings
Users using custom-call or multipart model mappings
Users using Replicate's independent image decomposition entry point
Domestic and overseas users whose preferred upload host has different reachability or account constraints

external_sources.purpose: KIE multipart stream upload and response contract
APIMart image multipart upload and 72-hour URL contract
fal CDN local upload and public URL behavior
fal official SDK upload implementation boundary
Replicate local file and input-file support
Runway ephemeral upload initialization and multipart contract
RunningHub binary upload endpoint and signed download URL
R2 free tier and storage cost boundary

invariants: Every local image, video, and audio reference is classified before upload and only sent to a declaration that accepts that media kind.
Every ordinary, custom-call, and independent Replicate entry point converges on the same asset localization resolver before paid generation submission.
A failed upload channel is retried only within the free upload boundary and then the next compatible channel is tried; paid generation submission is never wrapped by this retry.
Anonymous public hosting is never selected without the existing consent policy allowing it.
The target provider and other configured provider upload APIs are attempted before the optional Nomi relay; the relay is a controlled fallback, not the default storage destination.
R2 credentials stay in the optional server-side relay environment and are never embedded in renderer code or provider request bodies.
The relay refuses uploads that exceed its per-file, total-storage, or configured billable-storage budget; exact account operation charges remain visible in the Cloudflare billing dashboard.
generality_proof: The resolver is called by ordinary runtime mappings, custom-call preflight/dispatch, and Replicate decomposition. Its candidate list is derived from media capability and declared upload protocol, so adding or removing a provider changes one declaration rather than creating another caller-specific fallback. The shared executor owns JSON, multipart, raw PUT, auth, response extraction, and retry semantics for all candidates.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Select the compatible ordered channel list, including optional Nomi relay, configured providers, and consent-gated anonymous fallback.
Execute every declared upload strategy and reject invalid response URLs or provider-private values at the transport boundary.
Apply bounded retry classification only to free upload requests and rebuild request bodies per attempt.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Ordinary HTTP mappings call localizeAssetsForVendor before buildProfileHttpRequest.
Both custom-call preflight and dispatch use the same asset resolver and localization helper.
Replicate's independent file upload now uses the shared resolver rather than a separate upload contract.
This path validates local dependency existence and does not submit a provider request or upload a reference asset.

recurrence.reason: The same local-to-public transport failure can recur for every media type, provider, caller, network, and anonymous host; issue #237 already demonstrated a live anonymous-host outage.
same_class_scan: rg -n 'resolveLocalAsset|localizeAssetsForVendor' electron found runtime.ts, customCallDispatch.ts, image/decomposeLayers.ts and the shared resolver.
rg -n 'postMultipartForAssetUpload|file-upload|assetIngestion' electron found the shared localAssetFile executor and curated declarations.
Checked ordinary HTTP mapping, custom-call/multipart dispatch, and Replicate decomposition independently; all now use the shared boundary.

prevention.invariant: Only media-compatible, lifecycle-safe declared channels may be attempted, in a single deterministic order, before a provider request.
prevention.failure_mode: Unsupported media, missing relay configuration, expired/insufficient lease, invalid auth response, and exhausted channels fail with an actionable error and no paid submission.
prevention.strategy: Keep provider differences in AssetIngestion declarations and keep protocol execution in one resolver/executor; callers cannot invent a second upload fallback.

legacy_paths.rationale: The independent Replicate upload path is removed as a separate transport implementation; it now delegates to the shared resolver. Existing KIE/APIMart/anonymous declarations remain as declarations, not parallel caller implementations.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The implementation uses the existing fetch/FormData runtime and native Cloudflare Worker APIs; no new runtime dependency controls the invariant.

migration: Existing stored vendors and API keys remain valid. New curated vendor seeds are additive and idempotent. Existing projects keep local source assets and sidecars; remote objects are temporary and are not migrated. When NOMI_ASSET_RELAY_URL or its token is absent, the resolver preserves the configured-provider and anonymous chain behavior; when present, configured provider uploads still precede the relay.
residual_risks: The relay is live in the configured Cloudflare account; a custom public domain is not required for the current workers.dev deployment and remains a later presentation option.
Provider account eligibility, regional reachability, rate limits, and paid credits remain upstream conditions; the router can diagnose and move to the next channel but cannot grant eligibility.
The relay usage endpoint estimates storage cost only; Class A/Class B operation charges remain authoritative in the Cloudflare billing dashboard.
The provider model request contract still must declare the right input field/mode; upload success alone cannot prove a model mapping is correct.
